newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open unchanged to 1.00 cent per lb higher on Wednesday, as traders expected a technical correction following Tuesday's sell-off.
But some traders said the market could see some follow-through selling and suffer further losses.
"It's vunerable to the downside because of a lack of buying," said one trader. "There's just no paper there."

Tuesday, New York arabica futures ended sharply lower amid easing concerns about nearby supply tightness. September plummeted 11.15 cents, to 188.20 cents, after ranging between 204.00 and 185.50 cents. December fell 6.25 cents, to 168.50 cents, while the back months closed 2.85 to 4.80 cents lower.
The September/December switch shrunk to 19.70 cents compared with 24.60 cents at the close on Monday. December/March 1998 narrowed to 20.00 cents versus 22.10 cents the previous session.
Technically, traders said September resistance at 192.00 cents. On the downside, intial support was seen at Tuesday's low of 185.50 cents, followed by 182.50 cents.
On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday that no damaging cold weather is in sight for Brazil's coffee belt.

After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 227 60-kg bags as of August 11, to 93,565 bags. There were an additional 1,803 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

London robusta futures were weaker early Wednesday, but off lows. LIFFE November was down $9 at the midday break, to the session high of $1,528, after reaching a low of $1,500. Spot September fell $17, to $1,503.
